articles.title: What "production-ready" means for an AI-built app, in 32 checks
articles.excerpt: AI app builders make the demo path work in hours. I see it every week: a founder opens a Lovable, Base44, Bolt or Replit app, signs up, clicks through the main flow, and it works. The hard question co…
articles.body: AI app builders make the demo path work in hours. I see it every week: a founder opens a Lovable, Base44, Bolt or Replit app, signs up, clicks through the main flow, and it works. The hard question comes after that. In the words of the standard we published: "What decides whether an app can carry a business is everything the demo never tested: who can read which records, what happens when a payment webhook fails, whether a secret key shipped to the browser, and whether the owner can run the app without the builder." "Production-ready" gets used loosely, so we wrote it down. This post walks through what it means, one check from each area, and how to use the list before you launch or hire someone.
articles.author: Ahmed Hassan Yaseen

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built Inspiration & Interpretation of "Ghost in the Machine" Every day, millions of people open promotional, transactional, and service emails that are secretly haunted by automated algorithms: hidden unsubscribe labyrinths, confirm-shaming opt-outs ( "No thanks, I hate saving money" ), 1x1 zero-pixel tracking beacons logging IP addresses, and stealth auto-renewal clauses. These deceptive tactics are the invisible "ghosts in the corporate machine" —psychological traps engineered by automated systems to nudge, trap, and extract compliance from consumers. GhostProtocol flips the power dynamic.

articles.title: The OSI Model
articles.excerpt: The OSI Model Explained: What Really Happens When You Open a Website? By Naveenkumar Have you ever wondered what happens behind the scenes when you open Google, watch a YouTube video, or send a WhatsA…
articles.body: The OSI Model Explained: What Really Happens When You Open a Website? By Naveenkumar Have you ever wondered what happens behind the scenes when you open Google, watch a YouTube video, or send a WhatsApp message? You tap a button, wait a few seconds, and the information appears on your screen. It looks simple, right? But there is a lot happening behind the scenes. Your device needs to communicate with servers, send data across networks, identify destinations, and receive responses. Different networking technologies work together to make this communication possible. This is where the OSI Model comes into the picture. The OSI Model breaks network communication into seven layers. Instead of looking at networking as one complicated process, we can understand it step by step.

articles.title: Semantic HTML and Accessibility: What I Learned
articles.excerpt: When I started building my portfolio, I made every part of the page with tags. A is just a box, and it doesn't tell the browser what is inside it. Semantic HTML means using tags that describe what the…
articles.body: When I started building my portfolio, I made every part of the page with <div> tags. A <div> is just a box, and it doesn't tell the browser what is inside it. Semantic HTML means using tags that describe what the content is, like <header> , <nav> , <main> and <footer> . People who are blind use screen readers, and these tags tell the reader what each part of the page is, so they can jump straight to the menu or the main content. Search engines also understand the page better, and the code is easier to read. Alt text is another important part. It is a short description inside an image tag. Without it, a screen reader has nothing meaningful to read, so a blind person misses what the image shows.

articles.title: A system that is still becoming one thing — Simondon on individuation, and the plant's open states
articles.excerpt: A dashboard can show three things about the same observation. It can say the reading is fresh, it can say the reading is missing, or it can say the reading is UNKNOWN. The first two are settled. The t…
articles.body: A dashboard can show three things about the same observation. It can say the reading is fresh, it can say the reading is missing, or it can say the reading is UNKNOWN. The first two are settled. The third is a state that has not yet been decided. Nothing crashed, and nothing is confirmed healthy. The honest label is the uncomfortable one: not yet determined. Gilbert Simondon's Individuation in Light of Notions of Form and Information starts from a question that makes this kind of state more interesting than it first looks. We usually begin from finished individuals, a crystal, an organism or a machine, and ask how they are put together. Simondon asks how an individual comes to be at all, and what was there before it was one. This is the eighth piece in the philosophy series on this blog.

articles.title: An aquanaut comes home: Returning to Earth from an undersea 'space station'
articles.excerpt: After five days of living underwater, Analog Astronaut Commander Dr. Musilova and her crew return to terra firma, affected by higher pressures and the team's disconnection from home.
articles.body: Our time on our "space mission" underwater was coming to an end, and I felt like what I imagine an astronaut on the International Space Station (ISS) must feel before returning to Earth. On one hand, you are excited to return to your home and loved ones, as well as to fresh food and normal hygiene. On the other, you know you will miss your crew and the incredible experience of being in space. While my SEA STAR crew and I had not left Earth during our mission, we were separated from the surface of our home planet for five days. All we saw was a green alien water world surrounding us. We did this to live and work like astronauts on the ISS .

articles.title: India launches next-gen navigation satellite to orbit (video)
articles.excerpt: India launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite to orbit today (Oct. 30) atop a GSLV rocket. It was the fourth orbital launch from Indian soil so far this year.
articles.body: India bolstered its homegrown satellite-navigation system today (Oct. 30). A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time). Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff. An Indian GSLV Mark II rocket launches the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Oct. 30, 2026. (Image credit: ISRO) NVS-03 is the third next-gen satellite that India has launched for the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its version of the United States' Global Positioning System ( GPS ).

With this control, publishers can apply their AI training preferences across multiple AI companies, instead of setting them individually.
